utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around are the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecution versus Prlic et al., thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] Mr. Pusic is probably ill. I hope he gets better quickly. I would like to greet the counsel, Mr. Stringer, as well as all his associates, women associates since there are no men associates. I would like to greet them all. The registrar and the usher as well as all the people assisting us in the courtroom. Registrar has a few IC numbers to give us. This is today the 24th of November. I would like to greet everyone starting off with all the accused, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through witness Tomic, Neven. The list submitted by 1D shall be given Exhibit number IC 00889. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit number IC 00890; the list submitted by 3D shall be given Exhibit number IC 00891; the list submitted by 4D shall be given Exhibit number IC 00892; and the list submitted by the Prosecution shall be given Exhibit number IC 00893. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Last week the Trial Chamber handed down a decision relating to the expert witness who is coming to testify today. The examination-in-chief has been set to two hours and cross-examination by other Defence counsel to -- I believe it's Mr. Praljak and Mr. Petkovic's Defence counsel. In light of the scope of this testimony, has set the cross-examination time to three hours. This witness is coming to testify after Ewa Tabeau, whom we have already heard. I see that Mr. Karnavas is ready. He has given us his file with all the documents that will be presented. There are ten or so documents. We shall bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you give us your first name, last name, and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Svetlana Radovanovic, 14 November 1949.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a full-time professor at university.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... university.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the interpretation. The school of geography of the university in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ma'am, have you already testified before a court of law on those events that unfolded in the former Yugoslavia or is it the first time you come to testify today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You testified before which tribunal and in which case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've testified at this tribunal on four cases: The Galic case; the Blagojevic case; the Beara, Nikolic, and others case; and the Simic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you have testified in four cases. Were you a Prosecution witness or a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence witness. And I also testified at the court in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You testified in Sarajevo in which case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't be able to give you the number of the case or the name of the accused. I could only give you the name of the counsel, and the case had to do with genocide and Srebrenica. I -- to be more specific, it was the Kravica case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And were you a Prosecution witness or a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to read the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, ma'am. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just some information I would like to share with you so that this hearing unfolds in the best conditions possible. Since this is the fifth time that you are testifying before this tribunal, you know how things work out. You will first answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Karnavas, based undoubtedly on the documents he will show you. After that, other -- the other Defence counsel representing the other accused, since Mr. Karnavas defends Mr. Prlic, well, the other Defence counsel can also put questions to you as part of the cross-examination. The Prosecutor, who is on your right, Mr. Stringer, will cross-examine you when the time comes, when he has the floor. The four Judges that make up the Bench will put questions to you. This might be different from what happened in the other cases you testified in. In this case the Bench does ask a lot of questions. This is what you may feel is a bit different from what you have experienced in the other testimonies you gave. Please be as accurate as you can. Since you are a university professor I'm not concerned about this at all, and I'm sure you'll be able to sum up your answers in the best possible way. If, however, you do not understand a question, and even if it is a Judge that puts a question to you, sometimes the Judges don't put the questions as they should, in that case do not hesitate and ask the person who put the question to you to rephrase it, please. We have a break every hour and a half, but if at some point in time you don't feel comfortable or if you need a break, do not hesitate to raise your hand and ask us to have a break. We are quite prepared to do this. This is what I wanted to share with you, ma'am, so that this hearing can unfold in the best way possible in the interests of all of us and in the interests of justice. I'm very happy to give you the floor, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just to inform the Trial Chamber and the witness, the cross-examination is goes to be conducted by my colleague, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We will hear Ms. West with great pleasure also. We have already had the opportunity to hear you. We regret, however, Mr. Stringer, that you are not conducting the cross-examination yourself, but I'm sure we will have the pleasure to hear you at a later stage. Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President; good afternoon, Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Professor Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before I begin my first question, Your Honours, there was a technical matter that was brought to my attention just prior to coming into the courtroom, and that is Professor Radovanovic's report, which is 1D 03110, was not added to the 65 ter list, and therefore at this time I would be asking permission that it be added to the list so then I could make reference to it during my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This had been noticed by the Bench. I shall confer with my colleagues, but I'm sure it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber fully agrees to this. It is quite natural that this report be added onto your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President; thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Professor Radovanovic, in your report which we have, which is 1D 03110, attached to it there is an annex which has your CV, your curriculum vitae. Is that an accurate one, madam?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to go through all of your educational background because we can all read it, but suffice it to say you hold a Ph.D. from the faculty of geography, and as I understand it your speciality is demographics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do hold a Ph.D. in geography.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So let's just briefly focus a little bit on your work experience. If you could be so kind as to give us a brief overview of your work experience specifically related to the field of demographics, because after all that is what we are all interested in.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1974 -- or, rather, from 1974 to 1992 I worked in the National Bureau of Statistics of Serbia. As part of my job I worked exclusively in the department for population statistics. In 1986 I became the head of that department, and I participated in three population censuses. The first one was in 1971, and then I participated in the preparation, realisation, and processing of the 1981 census, and in that, in 1981, I was a member of the expert team of the then SFRY for the methodology of the census. In 1991 I also participated in the census as a member of the expert team for methodology. The expert team was composed of the representatives of all former states of Yugoslavia, and I was also in charge of the population census of Serbia. I would like to emphasise that the methodology --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Two points. One, you may need to speak a little bit slower, and, two, you may need to speak a little bit louder. That may be helpful. Slower and louder. Thank you. And my apologies for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All population censuses that were conducted in the former Yugoslavia were conducted according to a uniform methodology which was prescribed by the Federal Bureau of Statistics. In addition to the census statistics I was also involved and I headed the services for vital statistics, which means the services that were concerned with natality, mortality, marriages, and from 1982 I was also the head of the service --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You need to slow down. Otherwise, they can't -- you're going to wear them out. So please slow down. Keep in mind that this is simultaneous. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was part of the team that introduced the service for migration statistics. In 1992, I joined the institute of social sciences, the centre for demographic research, and that's where I worked on scientific projects that this centre was involved in. They were funded by the Ministry of Science and other institutions. I also headed two projects myself. I also participated in the following projects: The one of the European Centre for Peace and Development of the United Nations that studied the population of one part of Serbia known as the Raska Oblast region or Sandzak with a prevalent Muslim population. In 1992 -- or, rather, 1999, I apologise, I joined the faculty of geography, and since then I've been a member of the faculty of geography. I was the head of department for demographics, and for a while I was the deputy dean for finances of the school of geography. I teach three modules to regular students. One is introduction to demographics, population statistics, and ethnodemographics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm also --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought you were finished.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I also participated in a number of scientific and research projects that were conducted and are still conducted at the school of geography, and I have also participated in many projects that are conducted by the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences under the leadership of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences. I've organised and prepared the methodology for the interim census of the population of one part of Serbia known as Silic [phoen] county, and that is actually in the province of Kosovo and Metohija. I'm a member of the committee on population of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences and several other associations such as the Association of Geography, the Statistical Association, the Demographics Association and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think we have a pretty comprehensive overview of your -- of your background. Now, if I could turn your attention to this document, which is 1D 03110. That's the very first document in your binder. Do you recognise this document, madam?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. One moment. Mr. Karnavas, I have a follow-up question to put concerning this person's -- this witness's resume. I listened carefully to everything you have done. With your Croatian or Muslim counterparts did you ever work together on census projects as part of a cooperation programme with all the other republics, or did you only work on data concerning the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We worked together. The methodology that was established by the Federal Bureau of Statistics was our joint project which involved all the demographic statistics experts which implies census and vital statistics from various republics. Before you come up with an organisation and before you come up with a methodology, first you have to organise a group of experts that will be involved in the drafting of a methodology for the population census. Then that methodology for population census is published by the Federal Bureau of Statistics, and it becomes the only one and uniform for all the republics of the former Yugoslavia, and then that methodology was applied across the board. All of us had to carry out our censuses according to that methodology. I have to emphasise that the republics had the right to add some questions that they deemed important or interesting for their particular regions. The additional questions could differ, i.e., could only apply to one republic. Everything else was applied across -- across the board and had to be implemented in the same way, and this did not apply only to the methodology. It also applied to the organisation, the processing, the tabling programme and the programme of data publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this mean that today in all the existing republics the methodology is exactly the same, nothing's changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the information that I have from the republics, for example what happened in Croatia in 2001, as well as in Slovenia and Serbia, most of it is the same methodology. There are a number of questions which differ somewhat in Croatia from what has been done in Serbia. However, the key elements of the methodology have not changed, but I would like to add to that that these are very complex things, because a methodology involves a lot of things. It involves administrative and territorial division. Administrative and territorial division has not remained the same in Croatia. It is not the same in -- it was not the same in 2002 as it was in 2001. However, the instruments, such as nomenclatures for the coding of ethnic groups, for establishing various circles, professions, these have been changed. However, the essence of the methodology is still in place. It is still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for your very comprehensive answer. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, looking at this document 1D 03110, this is your report, is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us how was this report created. Who was involved in it? What was done in order to create it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You contacted me, and you asked me whether I would be interested in participating in that and whether I would like to look at the OTP experts' report that was drafted for this case, and then you sent me the report -- i.e., reports. We're talking about three reports, not just one. I read the reports, and then we spoke again. I gave you my opinion. I provided you my objections to those reports, and then you instructed me that I could peruse the original materials that were used by the OTP experts. You allowed me to come and inspect the materials, and you gave me free hand to inspect any other source of data in drafting my report for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And as a result of your work, how many reports did you produce? I know this is one, but there are how many parts to this report? What does it address?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I produced a report in two parts. I could have come up with three reports. However, a report on the wounded is something that I did not produce because it presents the same problems as the previous two reports. I studied that third report very carefully, and I'm absolutely able to answer all your questions with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you came here to The Hague to look at the data. Could you please tell us how long were you in The Hague and with whom and what exactly you did?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: With two assistants of mine, and they are IT experts, I spent between 14 and 18 April in The Hague in the demographics department of the OTP. I had at my disposal the main sources of data that had been used by the OTP expert and some other sources of data that I wanted to look at. I made sure that I was well informed with the contents of these sources and to draw my conclusions from those sources. I obviously could not peruse any other by the -- but the main sources of data. I could not dwell upon any of them in any more detail. However, I leafed through them in order to be able to spot the essence, to see how significant they were, why they were applied and how, and so on and so forth. From that exercise I was able to draw my own results, and in addition to that, I obtained most of the expert reports, particularly those that were relative to the ethnic structure. These were done by Dr. Ewa Tabeau. I perused those. And I also obtained a number of official publications that were published by the Federal Bureau of Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina. These are mostly statistics publications. And I have forgotten to say that I also obtained some publications that were published by the ministry for refugees and displaced persons. I have listed all the references and sources that I used in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We won't dwell on your report to any degree because we can all read it, but I will be asking you questions that relate to your report, but first it might be good just for housekeeping purposes to go through some of the other documents that are in the folder that apparently you used in addition to what was provided to you and what you looked at from the OTP list. If we could look at 1D 03099. That's the second document. If you could please tell us whether you recognise this document and, if so, what is it is and why is it relevant? It's the second document.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: 1D 030 -- I have as the second document 1D 03099.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct. 1D 03099.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please tell us what is this document then?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a publication issued by the Federal Institute for Statistics in Sarajevo, and it presents data canton by canton. There are separate sets of statistical data for each canton from several aspects of the statistics. What I was interested in was the data about the population, in particular the table of the ethnic breakdown. So there is the assessment of the overall number for the population with the ethnic breakdown. And I used several brochures put out for various cantons, because the municipalities that the Prosecution expert is dealing with can be found in various cantons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, why didn't you obtain this document, or did you try to obtain this document from Ms. Ewa Tabeau while you were here in The Hague examining the other material?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did write a request to you indicating what I would like to have at my disposal when I come to the demographic unit. These publications were listed in the request. However, I did not get those publications, and I concluded that they did not have those publications at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 03100, the next document. If you could look at it and please tell us if you recognise it and, if so, why it's significant.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a publication from the ministry for human rights and refugees, the sector for refugees of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it provides information about the situation in the field of the return of the refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina, displaced persons, and so on and so forth. It was published in Sarajevo in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is this an official document or unofficial?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's an official document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at the next document, 1D 03101. Do you recognise this document and, if so, what it is and why it was relevant.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's one of the brochures published by the Federal Institute for Statistics that I was talking about, and it pertains to the cantons in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This quite specifically is the Central Bosnia canton, and the title is "Central Bosnia canton in figures," and the reason why I used it is the table for the assessment of the number of the population with the ethnic background and because two of the municipalities -- or rather just one of the municipalities that are relevant that was analysed by the Prosecution expert, Gornji Vakuf, is in this canton.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document 1D 03102. If you could tell us what it is and why this is relevant.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is again an official document from the Ministry for Human Rights and Refugees. It was published in Sarajevo in 2003, and as you can see, the title is "Bulletin 2003," and it contains comparative data about refugees, displaced persons, and returnees, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But why was it necessary for you to look at this particular document?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this document speaks about the refugees and displaced persons and provides information municipality by municipality. And since the data pertained to the same census of the refugees and we have the database in the demographic unit of the OTP, I consider this to be quite important because it enabled me to follow this municipality by municipality in terms of refugees, displaced persons, and returnees, and so on. And I consider this to be the officially published data that are backed by the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina and its ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Having reviewed Ewa Tabeau's reports, do you know whether she makes reference to this particular bulletin that you indicate is, one, official and, two, is relevant, particularly to the period of time that we're interested in?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not notice her mention it anywhere at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at 1D 03103. If you could please tell us whether you recognise this document and, if so, what it is and why it's important.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, again this is the brochure for the Western Herzegovina canton, the canton in figures. It is again important because it provides the assessment of the number of the population by ethnic group, and there are municipalities here that were necessary for -- in order for me to be able to come to the total for the eight municipalities that Dr. Tabeau analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, prior to coming here to The Hague we had made a request for you to send some material by Federal Express at the request of the OTP. Are these some of the documents that the Office of the Prosecution was asking to look at, or were there other documents unrelated to the ones that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood it right --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again to save time. Prior to arriving here I had made a request for you to Federal Express certain material that was being requested by the Office of the Prosecution, material you had used and made reference to in your report. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do recall that. I was very much opposed to this request that you made because you asked me to send materials that had been officially published, and I replied to you twice that I was not asking the OTP to send the officially published materials to me, but then when you raised your voice I sent those materials to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And are these some of the materials that were being requested by the Office of the Prosecution, because one would assume that if they had them, they wouldn't be making the request.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume that the OTP does not have it since they're asking me to provide them with the officially published materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to listen to my question, and my question is very precise. Are these the material or some of the material asked?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not some but all of the materials that the OTP asked for, plus the instructions on the voters, which is not here, but I also sent it to the OTP because I used it in the drafting of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say the instructions on the voters, is that something that was used during the election to which Ewa Tabeau makes reference to or uses statistics from? Are we talking about that election?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the instructions for the registration of voters in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And Dr. Tabeau has the list of registered voters. I don't know whether she has also the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In your -- in your field of work would it have been useful, for instance, for Dr. Tabeau or this demographics department to have had that sort of information all of these years since they've been using that voter registration in virtually all of their reports?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What's the grounds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Mr. President, the rest of Your Honours and everyone in and around the courtroom. The question posed by Mr. Karnavas suggests the answer within it and it's leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're dealing with an expert. The question is would an expert rely on this sort of information. If the answer is yes, then it poses the question at some other point how on earth has Dr. Tabeau and the OTP demographics department been using these statistics all these years without getting the instructions and why it that Karnavas and his expert would now in 2008 have to provide that information. If the answer's no, I move on, although again if it wasn't relevant, then why would they ask for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Well, madam, could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question. I got a little bit lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question is: These instructions, is this something that would be -- is this material that would be relevant to a demographer such as Ewa Tabeau, especially since she's making reference to the electoral results or those elections in various reports throughout the years?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every instruction is an explanation of a part of the methodology. This instruction tells us how the voters lists were made, how voters were registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who can participate in the exercise, how to register, where to do it, how to register the location, where one wants to vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. If I could now get you to look at -- just glance at the next two documents. One is P 09836 and P 09837. Those are the last two documents in your binder, and I am going to ask you a leading question, which is: Are these the reports by Ewa Tabeau that you looked at and analysed and wrote your report on?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we discuss these reports, if you could very briefly, recognising that the field of demography is very complex and you're a professor, so we want a short, concise answer, not something long-winded, if you could just please tell us a little bit about demography, what it is and what are the tools that a demographer would use in carrying out their -- their work?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: A demographer has to have good quality sources for the data, must be able to classify the data and also to process the relevant statistical and demographic indicators and must be able to analyse the data and to reach some causal conclusions. The instruments that you use are what is called methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we speak about methodology, if you could -- and I'll try not to ask compound questions, especially if they are lengthy because then you may be answering only one part of the question. What is demography essentially?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: To cut a long story short, it's the science about population. It studies the size, the structure, the natural and territorial migrations or changes. It is a multi-disciplinary science, because in addition to its own methodology, it borrows methodologies from other sciences close to it, and just as it lets other sciences use its methodology and its results.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could go -- now we can talk a little bit about what you indicated, methodology. What do you mean by that, so that way we can identify what the terms are and use them consistently throughout the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, methodology is a complex set of procedures that you have to device and implement if you want to research a phenomenon, whether it be population or anything else in some other science. And this complex system of steps, as far as demography is concerned, can be divided into three steps, broadly speaking. The first step is the selection of the sources for the data, and this first step is actually the key step, the most significant one, because if you don't select your data sources, if you don't assess them and evaluate them properly, then your methodology may be perfect and you may be fully versed in various techniques of statistics, if the first step is not done properly, all the other steps that follow simply make no sense. The next step, the second step, is precisely this one: From your data sources you extract the data. You group them based on some of your features, the features that you're interested in, that you want to study, and then you do your calculations in order to obtain statistical indicators, statistical and demographic indicators, and then on the basis of those you reach statistical and demographic conclusions which are part of the analysis that you're conducting. And as you analyse this, you establish things. You comment on certain phenomena that you encounter. And, if possible, you apply the causal principle to see what the causes are, what the consequences are, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And these three general or major steps that you've indicated to us as part of the methodological processing in demographics, are they recognised within the field of demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now if we can start with the first one, and I'm going to ask you to be again short, concise, and very concrete. You indicated that sources, that the sources are important. What do you mean by sources? Could you give us an example, a definition and an example?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: A data source is something that a demographer uses. It is the basic -- the basis that you use in order to be able to produce some results. A data source is not something that is constructed by a demographer. A demographer usually knows where to go to get the best information about the population. Various statistics regarding the population, vital statistics, migration statistics. You can also study various monographs and other documents. So a demographer should be able to assess, to evaluate a data source that they intend to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And could you give us an example of a source? In this particular case what sort of sources were used, say, by Ms. Ewa Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau uses the 1991 census in Bosnia and Herzegovina. She used the voters list or electoral rolls from 1997 and 1998, and she uses the database on the displaced persons and refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we'll discuss that in greater detail, but I just want to go through the steps that you've laid out for us rather nicely, and as I understand it also, and I believe you said this was the very first step, you also used the word "key." Can you please explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the manner in which the OTP expert based on three data sources that are incongruous in terms of time resolved some issues, some problems she encountered in order to obtain her results. This is a methodological key that is called the matching, if that's what you meant. But if you want to say not the key but the key issue in methodology, the key issue in methodology is the selection and the proper evaluation and assessment of the data source. That's the key issue, because if you have a bad data source, you cannot have good results no matter your expertise. Demography and statistics of population have various keys, but there are also key issues in methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go to the next step. You said the next step is grouping and extracting of data. How is that done? Can you give us a brief overview?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Technically it is irrelevant what statistician or demographer we're talking about. The extraction of data, that means that you have to have a data source which enables you to establish the total number of a certain element, and then you want to classify this according to some features and analyse it. You can do that for each data source, and that's how it's actually done if your data sources are incongruous. But a different principle was applied here. Incongruous data sources were used --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- and on their basis the method that was used is well-known in statistics and in everyday life. Attempts were made to extract and group data from incongruous data sources as a product of a combination of those data sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again we're going to get to those reports. Right now I just want to get the general so we have a general foundation, so when we get to the reports we'll understand a little bit more precisely what it is you're saying. You did use the word "matching," and if you could please tell us what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Matching or the identification method or the matching method is a well-known method used not only in statistics and demography but in other sciences. It is in fact used in everyday life. It boils down to this: Through different data sources you can identify a single statistical unit. In this person -- in this case we're talking about a person. A very important thing when it comes to the matching method is to know what the matching key is. What is it? It is a series of elements that -- something that we will use to identify a person from one source in another source. For instance, the personal ID number, the unique personal ID number, is an excellent matching key provided it is correct. For a very simple reason, because it is unique, as its name tell us, and it contains elements that will guarantee that if you match it, if you match that key in two data sources, you will have the same person. That matching key has 13 elements. The first seven elements are the numbers indicating the day, the month, and the year of birth. The following two digits indicate the state or the republic and the area where the unique ID number was issued. The next three digits indicate whether it is a male or a female. And the last digit is the control digit, which makes it possible to prevent the duplication of the unique personal ID number. It renders it impossible to have two persons have the same ID number. This is the most precise matching key that you can have, but the sources that the Prosecution expert used did not have those ID numbers. There are ID numbers in voters lists and in the census numbers, but they are not correct. A large number of errors was noted, up to 40 per cent in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again I must caution you, we're going to get that particularly, but I first want to lay the foundation. Let's go to the third step, which is the analysis, and in that stage you indicated that you tried to draw some conclusions, determine some cause and effects. So could you please explain that a little bit to us.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: An analysis is the crown of any expertise, because it draws certain conclusions as to what happened. It ties causes to effects and explains what has been done. However, for any analysis to be good it has to contain analytical tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You're not finished, go ahead and finish.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is virtually no analytical tables in Ms. Tabeau's reports, which speaks of the scarcity of the sources that she used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's talk about those reports, and I won't go through them in any great detail, but the first report, for instance, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. There's a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I'm sorry for interrupting. There's something extremely important here. Professor Radovanovic, in order to do the matching, you need to have adequate sources, and you mentioned ID numbers. I heard this in English. I don't know how it was translated into French. And you are saying that the ID numbers which the Prosecution expert used were erroneous. This is what I understood. And your ID numbers were correct. Can you confirm this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have not explained it properly and that's why you did not quite understand. The OTP expert never mentioned having used ID -- citizens' numbers. I also did not use them. I only said that this is the best identification key. However, the problem of the sources used by the OTP expert lies in the fact that there is a huge number of mistakes among the IDs. Their percentage is over 40 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Radovanovic, if I have understood you correctly, in the former Yugoslavia, every citizen had a registration number. That's what you call a JMBG. If I have understood you correctly, this is a source which needs to be analysed when involved in demography. From what I understood, Mrs. Tabeau did not use these figures, this data. Is this right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again I have not explained properly. The fact is that every citizen of the former Yugoslavia did have the so-called JMBG, because in the 1980s a law had been passed on the JMBG. The JMBG was first collected in the 1991 census, and the underlying idea was for the former Yugoslavia to come up or to compile its population register. However, this unique personal ID number was not collected in a way that might be conducive to that. Over 40 per cent of people in towns and villages did not provide their ID number. That is why in the census data there is no ID for every person, nor is it consider data. It was not used for anything. It was never checked as such. When I was speaking about the matching method, I tried to explain and say that if the ID numbers were good and correct, then the matching method would guarantee reliable data drawn from the sources that do contain good IDs. The sources that were used for the analysis did not contain or did not show the satisfactory quality of the IDs in them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I have understood correctly, in 1991 when there is this census, the authorities hand out, I assume, a document to everybody, and this document should mention the acronym JMBG. The -- each citizen then hands in his filled-in document to the appropriate department. If I have understood you correctly, 40 per cent of the people at the time did not fill in the document properly or did not give in the document at all. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The ID number is given to every child who was born after the 1980s. When the birth certificate is issued to a child, it contains the child's ID. People who were born before the 1980s, before the ID was first introduced, they could not obtain any documents such as passport before presenting at the police and be provided with an ID. In 1991, the statistics wanted to start preparations for the introduction of the population registry. The preparation for the population registry would entail the collection of IDs from the population. And we did something that is not normally done in any census. They asked for -- from the interviewer, because you have to know that the censuses in the former Yugoslavia used the method of interview, which means that I as the interviewer would come to your household as a trained interviewer privy to the methodology, and I ask you to give me your data, and I also ask you do you have an ID, could you give me your personal ID documents so I could copy it -- from it? So it is the interviewer that enters the ID. Many citizens did not want to provide their IDs during census because they're not duty-bound to do so. I for one don't do that. I just give them the first seven numbers which reflect my date of birth. Some citizens are willing to provide their full ID; some are not. When the interviewers come, some citizens are not even there, so they could cannot provide their IDs. Some interviewers are not conscious and careful and diligent and they enter erroneous IDs. There was not an obligation. There is a law on census which provides exactly what needs to be collected and the citizens comply, but this was not one of those obligations. When all the data of the census was collected it was established in the statistics that ID numbers were collected from some 50 to 60 per cent in their complete form. As for the rest, either these IDs were missing the six last digits or they were erroneously recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, since we're speaking about the census in -- we got way ahead of ourselves a little bit, if you could just tell us, in the census there were also names. Now -- were there not? Names were collected. I'm talking about the census in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Names are collected, but they were never entered before 1991. And that was done only in some republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know why it was done in Bosnia-Herzegovina, for instance?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the reason lies in the fact that the material was scanned. The methodology of entering census data progressed with the progress of technology. The material was scanned, and when you scan a document you can automatically see the name. Serbia did things differently. Only the numerical data were entered. There are ladies who do that. So the first and the last names were never entered before the year 1991, and when this was done it was done only in some republics. The names were never entered onto the magnetic media. It did exist in the questionnaires, and they were never considered as census data, and indeed it is not one of the census data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, while I was talking about sources, let's at least at this point discuss the other two sources that were relied upon, at least for the one -- for the one study. And the second source, as I understand it, had to do with the voter registration. Could you please give us an overview of that. How was that compiled? How reliable is that as a source?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All the sources that were used by the OTP expert are incongruous. The census collects data for the entire population, and you know exactly the moment and how it is done. I'm trying to get to that. The registers of voters use a completely different methodology of data collection. The methodology that is used is on a voluntary basis. Every of-age citizen volunteers to vote or not, and if they volunteer to vote, they provide certain data, the first name, the last name. They can also provide their place of residence before 1991, and they also choose their polling station. They could register themselves or be registered by somebody else. They could even vote in absence. Registers of voters are not a source of data that to my knowledge have ever been used in scientific or professional research. They are considered unreliable not only in terms of their scope but also in terms of the fact that something can be provided and other things don't have to be provided. As soon as you have this arbitrariness the sources cannot be reliable. I've never heard of a register of voters ever having been used in a scientific or professional research as a source of data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what about the third source?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The third source of data originated from the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It could be accepted as an official source of data because it does contain -- it does contain a certain number of mistakes, but it has a key disadvantage. For two-thirds of the refugees and displaced persons it does not provide individual data, which is what Dr. Tabeau used. The only data it provides is for the head of the household. We know who the head of the household is and who the members of a household are. These data were collected from 1996 to 1998 by the local authorities and handed over to a certain place, and it was -- it was processed in 2004, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Karnavas. I believe we have a problem here. On page 29, line 25 of the transcript, in English it says: Registers of voters is a source of data. In French in the translation I heard, at one point in time I heard that the voters roll is the source referred to, and then I heard something else. Could you give us an explanation for this, please? You mean the voters roll is what you mean as not a reliable source?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. Lists of voters, voters rolls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ma'am, the difficulty I have, maybe it's the same for my colleagues, we as Judges, we were subject to a census in our countries, and we are on the list of voters, the voters roll. If we apply our own system, we are very surprised by what you are saying. It would be useful, therefore, for you to give us something with which we could compare. If you know, for instance, in Germany the voters roll is prepared in a particular way, and in the former Yugoslavia it is different, so that we can understand the differences better. The problem we have is that when we read the Prosecution expert, we read it through the eyes of what we are accustomed to, i.e., voters roll. You as a Defence expert, you say that this is not reliable and is of no interest. That's all very well. Maybe you are right, but what we would like to know is this: We would like you to give us some examples. For instance, if the voters roll in Gornji Vakuf is not an instrument that can be used to conduct a demographic analysis of the population, does this mean that the municipality had established these lists and this was on a voluntary basis and there was no obligation to register on these lists and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There's no obligation to register for voting. Entering your name on a voters list is your -- is up to you. It's a voluntary thing. As far as I know, all over the world, but I can't say that I know the entire world, I have never come across a single scientific or expert research that relied on the data obtained based on electoral rolls. What is absolutely possible is that the data from the electoral roll may be used to estimate the voters for a certain year, but the other way round, that the number of population is estimated on the electoral roll, I've never heard of that, especially when it comes to scientific and expert research. There may be some lay-research, but I wouldn't be aware of that. Electoral rolls, especially when it comes to this type of analysis, have another key shortcoming, and this has to do with the methodology used by Dr. Tabeau. They do not provide any data about the father, and they don't provide data about the ethnicity of the voter. How can they be used as comparative data for the calculation of an ethnic structure, and how can they be a reliable source for the precise identification of a certain person based just on the first and last names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood you correctly, as far as voters roll are concerned, if there was no obligation or legal obligation to register -- to register on these rolls in the former Yugoslavia, in other words only those people who wanted to registered, and if you conduct surveys on the basis of these voters roll, you run the risk of making quite a large number of errors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. There's no legal basis for that. There's no obligation to register. I know that there are some states like, for example, Greece, where it is different and everybody is obliged to register, but in the territory of the former Yugoslavia in 1997 or 1998, I'm sure that this obligation did not exist, and electoral rolls were established based on a voluntary registration of voters. In Serbia to this very day it is a voluntary exercise. You don't have to register if you don't want to. And I believe that the situation is the same in the other states of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you have just said is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me just follow up since you mentioned Greece, because normally in Greece one is registered where they're -- where they're born. What was the procedure in the former Yugoslavia as far as registering? Where would they register at? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I appreciate the reference to Greece, but I would just ask that counsel keep the facts coming from the witness and not from himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know how the registration was done in the former Yugoslavia, and did one have to register in a particular place and, if so, where?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean for voters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the eve of the election you are informed that you can go to your own municipality and check whether you are on electoral rolls. The electoral rolls were established in the past without any obligation upon you to go there and check. And then if you don't find your name, you have to query the situation. There are some local organisations that register the population, and censuses are very useful for that. I see in the census how many people they have and how many voters will vote. Otherwise there is no legal basis for somebody who is born to automatically become a voter in the place where they were born.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were there any other requirements such as being a resident in a particular place for a particular time?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, we're speaking about Bosnia. We're not speaking about anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to 1997 and 1998, there was no requirement. There was just a recommendation of -- of say to -- which said it would be good for you to say where you lived in 1991. And as for now, you can register at the place where you lived in 1991 or where you live now and left before April 1992, or you can register where you resided in 1991 or in the new municipality where you live now, or you can also register where you lived in 1991 or the new municipality, but if it's split then it's in its new part. There are very many either/or. In practical terms you could -- you had a vast choice of places where you could register for voting. You could register to vote in a place where you never resided or where you do not reside at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may. Ms. Radovanovic, is it possible to register at more than one place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that because I don't known what kind of control was in place. Whether somebody could be registered in Mostar, Sarajevo, I really don't know. I don't know what kind of checks they exercised at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ma'am, I am going to give you a concrete example. Let's assume we take the case of a Serb who is born in Gornji Vakuf. He is born to a mixed marriage. For instance, his father is a Serb and his mother a Croat. When he is 20, this man goes to work in Mostar and elections will be held. Can he register in Mostar, or does he have to register in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They can register in Mostar. In 1997 and in 1998 OSCE received voters registrations, which means I could come to a certain constituency and I could say, "This is where I want to register." And they gave you that possibility. They first tried to check where you were in 1991, and then they check why you want to register here. And then I could say, "Well, in April I -- 1991 I left and I've been here for a year," or I can say, "My parents moved and I want to join them in Mostar and that's the reason." OSCE tried to come up or establish completely new electoral rolls based on the population census, and these would reflect the population status at a certain moment, but it also provided a possibility to all people who were in Bosnia or who weren't because they were in foreign states to register. I personally know some people from Bosnia-Herzegovina who are residents of Serbia and they reside in Serbia. However, they registered to vote in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, in their municipalities or the municipalities where their parents resided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me take the last example before the break. Let's picture somebody who was born in Prozor and who at the age of 20 left to work in Germany, Frankfurt. But then during the holidays he comes to visit his parents who have stayed in Prozor. His parents tell him, "Well, there's an election coming up. It would be good if you could vote for so-and-so because we like this person." Now, in this case would -- could that person register on the list in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. His parents go to their constituency. They say, "Our son is abroad. He is a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and he has the right to vote," and they request that his name be put on the electoral roll. All citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, regardless of whether they were ever registered as voters, have the right to register and to vote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Let me make it a little more complicated. You've just said as he's a citizen, but let's say this young man is in Frankfurt and he got married to a German lady and he has become a German citizen through wedlock or because you've stayed enough years in Germany. Let's also imagine that he also has a German passport, but he also comes back to Bosnia because he has his family living there. Can he still register on the electoral roll, on the voters roll?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He can get all the documents of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the ID card, passport, and so on. The only condition is that he must not be at the same time a citizen of the State of Germany. In the former Yugoslavia it was impossible to renounce one's citizenship and then become a citizen of some other state. The regulations in the former Yugoslavia did not recognise dual citizenship, so you could have -- be a citizen of one state because you're not forced to renounce your citizenship in order to be a citizen of another state. And if Germany does not have this requirement that you have to prove that you renounced your BH citizenship in order to register as a -- to apply for a German citizenship, that person can have two passports. There are numerous examples. My granddaughter is a citizen of both Greece and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Two corrections. One on page 36, line 1. The example that was given is that her friend is a citizen of Serbia but voted in Bosnia and Herzegovina. She can correct me if I'm wrong. And on line 27, she indicated that one can be a citizen of Germany as long as they don't tell the state that they're -- as long as they don't tell Bosnia that they're a citizen of Germany they can still vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So perhaps the witness can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Those questions.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll try to make a clear record.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So your friend is a citizen of Serbia but voted in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1997 -- in 1998 he voted in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're just trying to be precise with the -- with the record, that's why. Secondly -- it may have been mistranslated because you're -- you might be speaking too fast. Somebody can be a citizen of Germany, have citizenship, a passport. As long as he doesn't tell the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he's capable of voting in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's what you were trying to -- that's what you indicated earlier, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the authorities never ask you that. So he can vote for as long as he doesn't say, "I don't want to vote because I am a citizen of another state." For as long as he keeps quiet about his other citizenship, he can vote in Bosnia-Herzegovina until the end of his life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... clear. I think it's about time to take a break, so we'll have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Professor, now if we could go to P 09836. Do you have that document with you? P 09836. This is the first report on ethnic composition and internally displaced persons, refugees. Do you have it, madam?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're not going to -- I'm not going to make any particular references to this, but I want to direct your attention that for the next half hour or so we'll discuss this, because I'll have another 30 minutes, perhaps, to discuss the other report and any other issues. I have an hour left of the two hours allocated for my direct examination. Now, if you could briefly tell us whether you found any problems concerning this particular report, keeping in mind, of course, that you already spent some time telling us that -- or reminding us of the three methodological steps that are important in the field of demography. So if you could please start with that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The problems in this report stem from the fact that errors are made in all three methodological steps that were to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... more concrete.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, the report is based on methodological incongruent data sources that contain a vast number of errors. The error margin ranges between 30 and 100 per cent. Secondly, the standard statistical and demographic methods were modified and adapted to the specific needs of this research. Thirdly, statistical and demographic conclusions were made on the basic -- on the basis of parameters which are not statistical and demographic indicators at all, and that is why we cannot speak about this as an expert and scientific report, as a report that would be acceptable from the point of view of its expertise and scientific value.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If I could start first with the first problem. You said that methodologically incongruent data sources. Why is that a problem, or how is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The census is an official data source. It is implemented by official organs using specific methodology, and the reason why I say it is a bad data source and why it is methodologically incongruent is because the expert uses first and last names from the census data, and they are not statistical data. They were not corrected in statistics, only in the demographic department. And the census entails making a list of all the population at the critical moment. The electoral rolls or voters lists represent persons who are legally of age and who volunteer to register. I don't know whether any official controls were carried out except for the fact that in the demographic unit of the OTP their names, first names and last names, were corrected. As I've already indicated, that's -- that covers the period of 1997, 1998. And in addition to a large number of errors made in the first and last names as they are listed there, I also mentioned that that is a systematic -- systemic error in statistical and demographic terms because there is no ethnic background listed there and no father's name. The databases on the displaced persons also contain a large number of errors when it comes to the first and last names, and there are no individual data for all those persons who are considered to be refugees and displaced persons. And in light of the fact that the Prosecution expert based her methodology on comparing individual data, then I can say that this database has an error margin of two-thirds. But as -- in terms of aggregate data, I consider this data source to be a valid one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Before we go to the second problem that you pointed out to us, are there any questions from the Bench with respect to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ma'am. I have a question about the margin of error. In your science, that of demographics, what is the percentage at which it is considered, the percentage of errors that it is estimated that a demographic report is reliable or not? So what is the acceptable error -- margin error which is agreeable by the international scientific community in your field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since demographics is based on the statistics of population, the population statistics, then the error margin is in line with statistics as a science and statistical analysis. Up to 5 per cent is tolerated. A datum is considered to be valid if we have the error margin up to 5 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say 5 per cent in terms of error margin. In Mrs. Tabeau's report, I understand that in your assessment there is a 30 to 40 per cent error margin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my assessment that it ranges between 30 and 100 per cent, but I have to explain why this range between 30 and 100 per cent. With the maximum degree of tolerance and given the great deal of effort put into correcting the names, I think that the minimum -- at the minimum, 30 per cent of the names couldn't be done properly. It is also a question whether they did it at all. And I have to underline that it is impossible to verify, to control this. If you have the database for the displaced persons as the aggregate data, then two-thirds of the persons for whom you don't have individual data, you only have the aggregate for the heads of the household and the members, you could not even verify that. But when I say up to 100 per cent, if you have the data source that does not contain the information that you're dealing with, for instance, the ethnic composition, in statistics it is considered to be a systemic error. Now, it is a whole different ball game if you start to construe that, but you have a data source that in 100 per cent of the cases does not contain the indicator that you use in your analysis later. The same goes for the father's name as a major parameter for a more accurate identification of a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I take it that you've also said what you just said today in the four other trials to which you were a witness and also for -- on the basis of Mrs. Tabeau's report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's what I said. It was not always about Dr. Tabeau's report. In one case it was about Dr. Brunborg's report. In another case Dr. Brunborg -- or, rather, Dr. Tabeau is a co-reference. She participated in it together with Dr. Brunborg, and in the other two cases Dr. Tabeau is the sole author, and that's what I said several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have the time to look again at the decisions. Of course I have read all of the decisions, but I haven't had the time to look at it in depth, but as far as you know, have you read the decisions in question about this discussion amongst experts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Radovanovic, there is something I have not quite understood, and maybe it is not correctly recorded. I go back for the others to page 41, line 4 to 7. You are recorded here as saying: "And in light of the fact that the Prosecution expert based her methodology on comparing individual data, then I can say that this database has an error margin of two-thirds. But as in terms of aggregate data, I consider this data source to be a valid one." Frankly, I simply do not understand what you are telling us here if that is what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is more or less what I said. In essence it is correct. The database on the refugees and displaced persons were set up in such a way that when those persons are registered or recorded you take all the information about the head of the household, if I may put it that way, and then you indicate the number of family members. So for instance, if you register Svetlana Radovanovic, I would provide all the personal details, the year of birth, ethnic background, place where I come from, and my family members would be registered together with me but you would not have the personal details for them. For instance, you would not have the indication of their ethnic background. Now, this database has one-third of all the data that pertain to the heads of the household, and for two-thirds you don't have the full information. So the comparison, the method used by Dr. Tabeau, although to be quite frank she resorted to using this database to the smallest extent, gives her an overview of all the material. As for the ethnic background of the refugees and displaced persons registered in this manner for the household members was determined by her on the basis of the ethnic background registered for the head of the household.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And you consider that to be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I believe that if you look at the aggregate data in this document in the database that it is correct in the aggregate, but if you apply the method that Dr. Tabeau applies, then you cannot look at all of that, because Dr. Tabeau needs to have individual data at her disposal, to look at the individual data. So I think that at the aggregate level the database is correct, it's valid, but it makes it more difficult to apply the methodology applied by Dr. Tabeau, because in two-thirds of the material she cannot actually do the matching.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a line -- there's a correction which might cause some confusion. On page 44, line 10, she indicated does not give her an overview of the numbers. So maybe -- I don't know if that is one of the things that you're focusing on, Judge Trechsel. It's not that it gives her, but it does not give her. That's what was indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add one more thing. The database on the refugees and displaced persons was used to the least extent by the Prosecution expert, but I considered it to be my duty to let you know what its deficiencies were. On the basis of the data extracted from the database on refugees and displaced persons, she obtained a single result. The Prosecution expert obtained one single result. All the other results regarding the refugees and displaced persons are obtained through the census and through the voters lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, going back, I mean Judge Antonetti asked you a question which I was going to get at later on, but I'll just ask you now. Within the scientific community, the method that was used by the OTP, and they continue to use over the years this methodology, if we want to call it that, is that acceptable within the scientific community in demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, but let me just say one thing. The methods used by the Prosecution expert exist. The matching method exists, but the Prosecution expert does not apply those methods in accordance with the standards that apply in scientific research. They are modified, adapting them to her research or his research.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if I could be a little bit more concrete, because on the first aspect, the first problem, you said that she used methodologically incongruent data sources. Is this something that is done within the field of demography, that you would take incongruent sources and try to match it in order to come up with some sort of a result that has meaning?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You don't take mutually incongruent data sources, but the Prosecution expert modifies that and brings the data sources which are not comparable at the aggregate level down to the individual level and then matches them in a way that fits her purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you give us an example so we can understand. When you say she modifies that, how does she modify it? And first let me ask -- perhaps I should ask: Is modification acceptable within the field of demography? In other words, does the demographer have the right to modify data within a particular source?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They do not have the right to modify the method that they use to obtain the data. If you modified the method, you automatically get modified data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you give us an example how that is done, because there may be this presumption that since therefore the OTP, this is a UN organisation, this must be an acceptable standard within the scientific community. So please tell us where it is or how it is that you differ with that opinion.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that they are methodologically incongruent data sources and that it would be methodologically unacceptable to, for instance, compare the age structure in 1991 and the age structure in 1997, 1998 at the aggregate level obtained from the voters lists.
